To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
preschoolers recognize domain-specific internal structures as early as age four, but their causal attributions do not reflect a detailed biological theory until later in development.
(1) children recognize domain-specific causal-explanation frameworks by age 4 and (2) children's causal attributions for biological events are initially anchored in an abstract, domain-general cause.

children's causal explanations of living and nonliving things develop in parallel, but children's knowledge of living things is more advanced than their knowledge of nonliving things, and this is because they have more detailed knowledge of the internal parts of living things.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of domain-specific explanatory frameworks, and the role of insides (e.g., internal parts) and immanence (e.g., the notion that an object is the cause of its own behavior) in these frameworks.
the development of causal-explanatory understanding in children.
the nature of the causal-explanatory knowledge that young children possess about the behavior of living and nonliving entities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of causal-explanatory knowledge is domain-specific, but the development of causal attributions is domain-general.
the development of domain-specific knowledge of biological internal parts is not accompanied by an equally comprehensive and detailed domain-specific causal theory.
the children in these studies were not yet ready to endorse a causal-explanatory framework for the domain of biology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the causal-explanatory framework for biological events develops gradually, with children's causal attributions becoming more sophisticated as they acquire a more detailed biological theory.
children have knowledge about insides and immanent causes but that this knowledge does not yet cohere in a coherent causal explanatory framework.
children's causal-explanatory knowledge is organized into domain-specific frameworks, which develop gradually as children acquire knowledge of internal parts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children are sensitive to domain-specific causal explanations as young as 4.
children’s causal-explanatory knowledge is not a unitary phenomenon but instead is domain-specific and develops over time.
the development of children's understanding of causality is domain specific and that the domain-specificity of children's causal explanations develops over a long time.
